assertions.text: Item operations (add/remove) are represented as their own table or tables — separate from coupon and cart total logic.
assertions.evidence: Two dedicated sections: '## Add Item to Cart' and '## Remove Item from Cart', separate from Coupon, Cart Total, and Checkout sections.

assertions.text: Coupon application (entering, replacing, rejecting codes) is represented as its own table — separate from item operations and cart total calculation.
assertions.evidence: '## Coupon Application' with dedicated table, distinct from item/total sections.

assertions.text: Cart total calculation (how different coupon types affect the price) is represented as its own table — separate from coupon application and item operations.
assertions.evidence: '## Cart Total' section with dedicated table showing price calculations by coupon type.

assertions.text: Checkout (stock verification) is represented as its own table — separate from the other concerns.
assertions.evidence: '## Checkout' section with dedicated table for stock verification logic.

assertions.text: Each table row is independently executable — no row depends on a prior row's result. The table expresses rules, not a sequential test script.
assertions.evidence: Each row in all tables shows a complete state transition (before/after or input/output) without dependency on prior rows. For example, 'Add to empty cart' doesn't depend on prior rows.

assertions.text: Item operations cover at least: add to empty cart, add to non-empty cart, add more of an item already in cart, remove item from cart, remove last item in cart, remove item not in cart.
assertions.evidence: Add Item covers: 'Add to empty cart', 'Add a different item' (non-empty), 'Add more of an item already in cart'. Remove Item covers: 'Remove one of several items', 'Remove the only item', 'Remove item not in cart'.

assertions.text: Coupon application table covers validity and replacement — not coupon types. Scenarios include at least: add valid coupon (none active), add valid coupon (another active), add expired coupon (none active), add expired coupon (another active), add nonexistent code (none active), add nonexistent code (another active).
assertions.evidence: Coupon table has 8 rows: valid (SAVE10, TENOFF, WIDGET5 applied), replace valid (SAVE10→SAVE20), expired (no coupon), nonexistent (no coupon), expired (with coupon), nonexistent (with coupon).

assertions.text: Cart total table covers how different coupon types affect the price. Scenarios include at least: no coupon, percentage off whole cart, fixed amount off, fixed amount exceeding cart total (floors at zero), product-specific discount (product in cart), product-specific discount (product not in cart).
assertions.evidence: Table includes no coupon, percentage, fixed amount, fixed > total (floor), product-specific (in cart), but lacks product-specific when product NOT in cart.

assertions.text: Checkout table covers at least: empty cart, all items in stock, and not all items in stock (insufficient inventory).
assertions.evidence: Checkout table: 'Empty cart', 'All items fully stocked', 'Exact stock match', 'One item one unit short', 'One item completely out of stock', 'Multiple items short'.

assertions.text: Column names use business/user-perspective language (e.g. 'Message?' not 'Result?', 'Coupon code' not 'input'). The tables read as a specification a product person could review.
assertions.evidence: Coupon table uses 'Current coupon', 'Code entered', 'Active coupon after?'. Checkout uses 'Checkout allowed?', 'Stock available'. Business-readable throughout.

assertions.text: Test data that affects the outcome — product prices, coupon rules (type, amount, expiry) — is visible in the table via columns, notes, or explicit setup, not silently hardcoded. The reader can trace how inputs lead to outputs.
assertions.evidence: Cart Total table: 'Widget ×2 (£10 each), Gadget ×1 (£25)'; coupon values '10%', '£10', '£5', '£50'; Coupon table 'Code status' shows rules like 'valid, 10% off cart'.

assertions.text: Multiple open questions are surfaced — ambiguities or product decisions the requirements don't specify (e.g. what happens to a product-specific coupon when that product is removed, or how percentage and product-specific discounts interact).
assertions.evidence: Multiple open questions listed: accumulation vs replace, quantity 0 validation, removal messages, product-specific coupon per-unit vs line-total, multiple-item shortfall messages.

assertions.text: Cart totals are arithmetically correct: sum(quantity × price) − coupon = total, for every row in the total calculation table.

Coupon application table uses a column to signal expiry status — either an 'Expired?' yes/no column, a 'Status' column, or equivalent. Expiry is visible per row, not just implied by the scenario name.
Coupon application table uses before/after columns (e.g. 'Active coupon' / 'Active coupon after?') to specify the state change when entering, replacing, or entering invalid coupon codes.
assertions.evidence: Coupon table has 'Current coupon' (before) and 'Active coupon after?' (after) columns.

assertions.text: Scenario names describe the business situation (e.g. 'Add more of same product', 'Replace active coupon') — not 'Test case 1' or generic labels.
assertions.evidence: Scenarios: 'Add to empty cart', 'Remove the only item', 'Replace an existing coupon', 'Fixed coupon larger than order total'—all business-descriptive.

assertions.text: Multiple tables (or @TableTest methods) are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing unrelated rules. Acceptable to use a single table only when the domain genuinely has a single concern.
assertions.evidence: Five distinct tables: Add Item, Remove Item, Coupon Application, Cart Total, Checkout.

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns. Fewer rows per table is expected when concerns are properly separated.
assertions.evidence: Each table: Add (4 rows), Remove (3 rows), Coupon (8 rows for 2×3 state/validity combos), Total (6 rows), Checkout (6 rows). No permutation bloat; rows address distinct rules.
